title: A TESS flare response model gives similar size slopes for CPV hosts and other rapid rotators
abstract: We test whether the known flare-rate excess in complex periodic variable (CPV) hosts includes a different flare-size law. A conditional measured-size model uses 846 host flares, 2,683 comparison flares and 65,660 published artificial trials. It allows an arbitrary rate normalization in each sector and includes measured-size migration. Under the primary power-law and width assumptions, the differential equivalent-duration exponent is 2.238 in hosts and 2.205 in comparison stars. The difference is +0.034, with a 95% paired star-bootstrap interval of -0.076 to +0.147 from 500 draws. Changes to the size cut, width law and untested high tail give small point differences. Thus the selected data show no clear host change in size slope. This is consistent with the prior rate excess being a normalization difference, but does not prove that origin. The fixed flare template, noise pooling, assumed size-width relation, selected sample and untested tails limit the inference. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included.

display.caption: Measured ED fractions and model size-slope tests. Only the primary comparison has a paired star-bootstrap interval; other rows are point sensitivity tests.
